headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risk from shared file/MCP workflows; no direct evidence of a dangerous default bridge.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher ingests web content, local documents, and MCP/API outputs; MinerU parses PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, OCR text, and exposes an MCP server. If MinerU output is fed into gpt-researcher as trusted research material, prompt-like text can be misread as instructions. The pairwise bridge is documented only indirectly, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into gpt-researcher prompts or files without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP workflow passes extracted text as trusted instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU output into prompts.
Add a fixed delimiter/template around extracted text.
Require human review before re-prompting on extracted documents.
Restrict MCP tools to read-only, provenance-tagged outputs.
requires-engineering: add content provenance and instruction/data separation.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher handles secrets and broad network egress, while MinerU is offline/private but can read local document inputs and expose them through API/MCP. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive documents or citations can flow from MinerU into gpt-researcher and then out via third-party APIs. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same local directory, document contents can be exposed to gpt-researcher.
IF gpt-researcher sends those contents to external APIs, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Remove secrets from the shared directory.
Turn off external API calls for sensitive runs.
Export only redacted excerpts from MinerU.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; MinerU cannot write files, modify git, or spawn subprocesses, and its network is allowlisted. Overlap exists mainly on read-side document handling, so direct write/write conflict is limited. Because the pairwise interaction is only partially documented, I keep this low rather than none.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory, gpt-researcher may overwrite artifacts created by other tools.
IF an orchestrator grants MinerU write access beyond its profile, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run gpt-researcher after MinerU finishes.
Keep MinerU in read-only mode.
Avoid shared git working trees.
requires-engineering: add lockfiles or workspace leasing.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations; MinerU extracts structured text from documents. A common workflow is MinerU output feeding gpt-researcher, which may then summarize or act on it without verification. That creates a plausible cascade from extraction errors to incorrect downstream reports, but not an automatic action-taking chain, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF MinerU extraction errors are passed into gpt-researcher as authoritative facts, downstream reports can be wrong.
IF gpt-researcher publishes citations without cross-checking source documents, the error propagates.
mitigations: Require source-document spot checks.
Compare extracted tables against originals for key fields.
Mark MinerU output as untrusted in prompts.
Add a second-pass verifier before publication.
requires-engineering: implement citation-to-source validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and show no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch. gpt-researcher does use third-party APIs and secrets, while MinerU advertises private/offline operation, so compliance friction is possible if regulated data is routed through gpt-researcher. The evidence is insufficient for medium, so low is the safer choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through gpt-researcher to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be implicated.
IF MinerU output contains sensitive data and is retained in shared logs, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of external API prompts.
Review retention settings for both tools.
Use redaction before export.
Document data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: add policy-aware routing and retention controls.
